orders.text:
IA No. 1873 of 2019 
In 
WPSS No. 3845 of 2018 
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Davesh Bishnoi, Advocate for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel for the 
State of Uttarakhand. 
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for 
respondent Nos. 4 and 5. 
Misc. Application No. 1873 of 2019 
filed along with supplementary affidavit by 
the petitioner is allowed. Supplementary 
affidavit is taken on record. 
The Coordinate Bench of this Court on 
16th November, 2018, have granted three 
weeks’ time to file counter affidavit to 
respondent Nos. 4 and 5. Till date, no counter 
affidavit has been filed by respondent Nos. 4 
and 5 and the petitioner is on the verge of his 
retirement. 
The argument, as extended by the 
learned counsel for the respondents is that the 
records are not retrievable. Since the matter 
pertains to 2010, some more time is required. 
This cannot be an excuse for delayed filing of 
the counter affidavit. Being an employer, it is 
expected that respondent Nos. 4 and 5 are to 
be equipped with the records of the petitioner 
/ employee. 
Learned counsel for respondent Nos. 4 
and 5 prays for and is granted two weeks and 
no more time to file their counter affidavit. 
List on 18th March, 2019. 
 
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 
Dated 26.02.2019 
Shiv

orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma
orders.text:
WPSS No. 3845 of 2018
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Davesh Bishnoi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Narain Dutt, Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for private 
respondent(s).
The petitioner, who has now a superannuated teacher, 
has filed this writ petition, claiming for certain arrears of 
salary and hence, he has modulated his reliefs in the 
following manner:-
“i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to 
grant the overdue claims of petitioner’s salary from 
the date when the same fell due; pay the arrears;
ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to 
calculate and pay the claims of petitioner’s salary 
from the date when the same fell due, as arrears, 
along with interest thereon;”
Apart from various factual aspects as involved 
adjudication, he has contended that when he was in service, 
he had raised a claim with regards to the payment of salary 
for the aforesaid defaulted period by filing a representation 
before the management, supported by the recommendations 
made by the Chief Education Officer, one of the reference, 
the same finds place in his representation dated 24.09.2018 
made before the Manager, where he has referred a 
communication, made by the Chief Education Officer dated 
13.08.2018.
Before venturing into considering the main relief, by 
way of a writ of mandamus, this Court is of the opinion that 
it wZxcould be apt to direct the petitioner to file a detailed 
representation with all the recommendation(s) and 
communication(s), as made by the Education Authority and 
submit the same before the Manager concerned within a 
period of two weeks from today. He can file a representation 
in relation to the salary in dispute apart from any other dues
payable to him. 
The Manager concerned is directed to take a decision 
on the same within a period of one month thereafter and 
place the said order on record of the present writ petition.
List this matter after six weeks.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 02.12.2019 Mahinder/

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that 
in compliance of the judgement, as passed by the 
Division Bench of this Court on 18.07.2018, he

payment of the benefit, as prayed for by him in the 
writ petition on 01.08.2018.

counsel for the petitioner informs that on the basis of 
said representation, the respondents had issued an 
order dated 23.01.2020, assigning reasons for their 
inability to pay the amount.
This Court is of the view that the said document 
is to be brought on record, in order to judiciously 
scrutinise the reasons for denial, for which the learned 
counsel for the petitioner prays a week’s time to place 
the same document on record.
The same is granted.
Learned counsel for the petitioner to place the 
said document on record either by way of 
supplementary affidavit or by way of an amendment, 
challenging the same as the case may be.
List this matter after one week.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)

Misc. Application No. 6669 of 2020, along 
with supplementary affidavit filed by the 
petitioner is taken on record. 
Misc. Application No. 6669 of 2020, 
accordingly stands disposed of. 
During the course of argument, what is 
revealed is that the petitioner has contended that 
despite of fulfilling all the formalities for 
remittance of the pensionary benefits, the same 
has been denied by the order dated 23rd January, 
2020, by the respondents on the pretext that the 
petitioner has not fulfilled the conditions. 
Since the petitioner’s argument is that he 
has fulfilled the conditions and the reason for 
rejection is erroneous, in such an eventuality, the 
petitioner would have to challenge the order dated 
23rd January, 2020, by seeking an appropriate 
amendment along with appropriate pleadings, for 
which, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays 
for that he may be granted a week’s time. 
The said prayer is granted. 
He may file an appropriate application as 
permissible under law. 
List this Writ Petition thereafter.

orders.text:
WPSS No.3845 of 2018
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Davesh Bishnoi, Advocate for the 
petitioner.
Mr. M.S. Bisht, Brief Holder for the 
State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for 
respondent nos.4 & 5.
Prior to attaining the age of 
superannuation, the petitioner was called 
upon by the Principal Kisaan Intermediate 
College, Peerumadara, District Nainial, vide 
his communication on 18.12.2018 to fulfill 
the certain documentary requirements for 
the purposes of processing his pensionary 
papers. The petitioner contends that by 
virtue of the response of 07.05.2019, he 
has supplied those documents.
But further the counsel for the 
respondents submits that after attaining 
the age of retirement, the petitioner was 
yet again called upon by the respondents to 
complete the additional formalities, which 
were necessarily required to be fulfilled 
after attaining the age of retirement, which 
according to the respondents has not been 
fulfilled by the petitioner. There is no such 
document on record, as such, placed by the 
respondents to show that they have called 
upon the petitioner and he has not 
responded to it.
The counsel for the respondents is 
directed to place the said communication 
on record, in order to enable the Court to 
pass further orders for the purposes of 
processing his pensionary papers. The 
same would be complied with by the  counsel for the respondents within a period 
of two weeks.
List this writ petition on 10.03.2021.
 
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 23.02.2021
Arti

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS No.3845 of 2018
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Davesh Bishnoi, Advocate, for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. M.S. Bisht, Brief Holder, with 
Mr. Gajendra Tripathi, Brief Holder, for the State 
of Uttarakhand/respondent nos.1 to 3.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate, for the 
respondent nos.4 and 5.
This Court on the previous dates had sought 
certain queries, which is to be provided by the
respondents. 
Today, when the matter was taken up for 
final adjudication, the learned counsel for the 
respondent nos.4 and 5 Mr. Sudhir Kumar, had 
submitted that the Principal of the Intermediate 
College, in which, the petitioner was initially 
working and from where he has attained the age of 
superannuation and retired from service. On 
31.12.2019, the Principal of the Intermediate 
College has written to the petitioner to approach to 
his office to clarify certain defects, which the 
Principal was facing for the purpose of processing 
his application for grant of the pensionary 
benefits. 
Learned counsel for the respondents has 
submitted that the nature of observations made in 
the communication dated 15.11.2019, required the
verification, for which the personal appearance of 
the petitioner and his wife, were required to 
appear before the Management, in order to enable 
the Management to process the application of the 
petitioner for pensionary benefits. 
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, learned counsel for the 
College submits that instead of appearing in 
person before the Management, the petitioner did  respond to the aforesaid letter vide his 
communication dated 06.12.2019, but that in itself
would not suffice, the purpose for which, the
Letter No.169 dated 15.11.2019, was issued by the 
Principal, because of the absence of the personal 
appearance of the petitioner and his wife, the 
documents cannot be processed, because other 
codel formalities are to be completed. 
To tied-away such peculiar circumstances 
and considering the fact that the petitioner has 
attained the age of superannuation and retired 
from service on 31.12.2019, and is claiming for 
the grant of pensionary benefits, an exception is 
carved out in the following manner:-
(1) That the petitioner would ensure to appear 
before the Management of the respondent 
College, along with his wife on 05.04.2021, 
to complete the formalities. 
(2) The respondent College and its 
Management is directed to fulfil all the 
formalities of processing the documents for 
pensionary benefits, including the 
verification of the petitioner and his wife, 
which is required for processing pensionary 
documents. 
(3) As soon as the said process is over, the 
Management would ensure to forward the 
papers/documents of the petitioner further 
to the superior authorities for the purpose of 
processing of pensionary benefits of the 
petitioner within a period of one week 
thereafter.
List this writ petition on 19.04.2021.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
22.03.2021
NR/

The learned counsel for the petitioner

WPSS No.3845 of 2018
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Davesh Bishnoi, Advocate, for the 
petitioner.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Additional CSC, for the 
State of Uttarakhand. 
The petitioner had attained the age of 
superannuation from the services of the 
respondent on 31.03.2019. 
During the pendency of this writ petition, 
an issue was raised by the petitioner with 
regards to the non settlement of the retiral 
benefit, which was being deprived to him. But 
later on, the facts which has been placed on 
record by the respondent, were that they have 
submitted, that the Committee of Management
had already processed the documents of the 
petitioner for the remittance of the retiral 
benefits, including the pension, and the same 
has already been referred to the Chief Treasury 
Officer, but since the Chief Treasury Officer 
was sitting over it, and no decision has been 
taken, the matter was placed today with an 
observation made by this Court in the order 
dated 15.11.2021, directing the learned 
Additional CSC to complete his instructions; as 
to what action has followed for the purposes of 
the remittance of the retiral benefits to the  petitioner, as it continued to be determined on 
the basis of the observations made by this Court 
in its order dated 19.04.2021, onwards. 
Learned Additional CSC has submitted 
that on the basis of the instructions, which he
has received from the office of the Chief 
Education Officer, Nainital by way of his 
communication No.8086, dated 17.11.2021.
The documents which was sent to the Chief 
Treasury Officer by the Management of 
Institution of petitioner for processing the 
retiral benefits of the petitioner. There were
certain objection, which were raised by the 
office of the Chief Treasury Officer vide its 
communication dated 30.10.2021. It is stated by 
the Chief Education Officer, that those defects 
had now been rectified and the documents of 
the petitioner for the purposes of the remittance
of the retiral benefits has been referred back to 
the office of Chief Treasury Officer, to be 
processed in accordance with law, but no 
decision as such has been taken so far after the 
rectification of the defects, which has been 
pointed by the communication of 30.10.2021.
In that eventuality, while keeping this 
writ petition pending, and considering the 
response received by the office of the Chief 
Standing Counsel on 17.11.2021, I am of the 
view, that in view of the rectification of the 
errors which was pointed by the Chief Treasury  Officer, since they now stand rectified in fact 
there could not be any practical impediment for 
the Chief Treasury Officer, now to process the 
documents of the petitioner for the purposes of
remittance of the retiral benefits.
For the reasons aforesaid, it is hereby 
directed that the Chief Treasury Officer in 
continuation to the communication made by the 
Chief Education Officer on 30.10.2021, would 
ensure to complete the documentation and 
process the retiral benefits and pension of the 
petitioner within a period of ten days’ from 
today and inform the Court accordingly. 
Put up this writ petition after ten days. 
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 17.11.2021
NR/
